invariants.assessment: No kernel fork or alternate SWAP implementation is introduced.
No file I/O is introduced into kernel production code; test fixture uses typed in-memory runtime inputs.
Parameters, forcing, committed state, numerical config and results remain distinct typed objects.
No new persistent column state is added.
No solver scratch is moved into persistent column state.
No production memory layout changes; existing runtime composition is consumed unchanged.
Both intervals run through the existing transactional serialized runtime and only committed results are chained.
No warm-start or rerun semantics are changed.
Case uses generic numeric t0, tm and t1 with no day or midnight assumption.
No coupling-window restriction or calendar coupling assumption is introduced.
Groundwater coupling runtime is not modified or claimed.
This is not direct SWAP-MODFLOW coupling evidence and makes no H_SWAP/H_MF interface claim.
Complete interval mass ledgers and a combined full-window hard mass gate are mandatory; lost-water tolerance is forbidden.
No interface-sensitivity contract is modified.
No coupling solve-count policy is modified.
Existing serialized MultiSWAP-capable runtime is used; no per-column heavy solver ownership is introduced.
No MODFLOW tile mapping is introduced into SWAP.
No deep-vadose component is introduced into SWAP.
No component transition or storage transfer rule is changed.
Test consumes the common soil-water solver contract through the current reference Full Richards implementation.
Existing drainage and Richards physics are composed without duplicating their functional implementation.
Drainage receives an explicit hydraulic view and does not inspect HeadCalc internal arrays.
Physical drainage activation and prescribed-head boundary are separate from the numerical transaction configuration.
No bounded-cost or fallback policy is changed or silently relaxed.
The current reference Full Richards runtime remains the numerical reference path; no reduced physics is substituted.
Case records mass, boundary, drainage publication and response diagnostics; existing solver diagnostics remain available.
No optional production module is made mandatory and no inactive-option state is added.
The runtime composes drainage inputs outside the kernel through the existing DIVDRA runtime wrapper.
No .swp parsing, midnight start, one-day duration or MODFLOW dependency is assumed by the case.
This file explicitly audits every architecture invariant for the workunit.

conclusion: F-TB10 introduces no adverse architecture delta. Its positive claim is restricted to scientific qualification of the specified TB09-003 interaction on unchanged current-canonical production code, conditional on exact-head CI success.
